statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107496 ("Infinite Loop in CMS_encrypt() With an EC Group Order of 1", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt . The fix is commit a0051cf, which makes EC key generation in crypto/ec/ec_key.c fail with an invalid-group-order error when the group order is 1 or less, instead of retrying without limit: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/a0051cfe699bf5a047bc1c4faef65f80f7987366 . The advisory states that the OpenSSL 3.5 FIPS provider is not affected. The DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl builds are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1, 3.5.9-r2 and 3.5.9-r3. 3.5.9-r2 is OpenSSL 3.5.9 rebuilt with that commit applied, and 3.5.9-r3 is built from Alpine's 3.5.9-r1 recipe, which carries the same change: https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json . We checked libcrypto in every build on x86_64 and aarch64, using the debug symbols in openssl-dbg matched by build ID, and the static libcrypto.a in openssl-libs-static. In 3.5.9-r2 and 3.5.9-r3, ossl_ec_key_simple_generate_key(), into which the changed ec_generate_key() is inlined, is larger than in 3.5.9-r1 (451 against 370 bytes on x86_64, 460 against 384 on aarch64), and in the static library it gains the fix's BN_cmp() and BN_value_one() comparison and error-raising calls, which 3.5.9-r0 and 3.5.9-r1 lack. 3.5.9-r0 and 3.5.9-r1 (a DHI rebuild) are OpenSSL 3.5.9 without the commit, and every earlier build is OpenSSL 3.5.8 or older, which does not contain it.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107496 ("Infinite Loop in CMS_encrypt() With an EC Group Order of 1", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt . The fix is commit a0051cf, which makes EC key generation in crypto/ec/ec_key.c fail when the group order is 1 or less instead of retrying without limit: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/a0051cfe699bf5a047bc1c4faef65f80f7987366 . Debian lists trixie as vulnerable with no fixed version: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107496 . DHI backports that commit into its standard Debian 13 openssl builds, starting with the second DHI build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and in every later standard build, including both DHI builds of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. On amd64 and arm64, those builds' libssl3t64 has a larger ossl_ec_key_simple_generate_key(), into which the changed ec_generate_key() is inlined (for 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, 545 against 469 bytes on amd64 and 520 against 440 on arm64; for 3.5.9-1~deb13u1, 529 against 453 and 504 against 436), compared with the first DHI build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and with the FIPS build of the same Debian version, read from the libssl3t64-dbgsym debug symbols matched by build ID; the static libcrypto.a in libssl-dev has the same sizes. Their changelogs also carry the backport entry. Every earlier standard build has the smaller function and no changelog entry: Debian has not shipped the fix, and DHI added the backport with the second 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build. The FIPS builds of openssl (the +fips versions in the DHI security repository) are affected: the FIPS build is pinned to the validated upstream release and does not take this backport. Their libssl3t64 has the smaller, unfixed ossl_ec_key_simple_generate_key() on both architectures in every FIPS build, and their changelogs have no entry for this CVE. The advisory's "FIPS impact: no" covers the FIPS provider module only; the affected code is in libcrypto, which the FIPS builds ship without the fix. A FIPS build sorts above the standard builds of the same Debian version, so the range has three affected spans: every build below the first fixed 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build, the 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 FIPS build up to the first 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 build, and the 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 FIPS build onward.
